extracted.intended_audience: small refineries, regulated parties, industry counsel, environmental law practitioners, and stakeholders affected by RFS SRE decisions
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures EPA uses to evaluate petitions for Small Refinery Exemptions (SREs) under the Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS), including the statutory basis for DEH, deference to DOE's matrix, implementation of exemptions (including treatment of retired RINs), and rules for judicial review venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small refinery definition (CAA 211(o)(1)(K))
rubrics_metrics.description: The CAA defines a small refinery as “a refinery for which the average aggregate daily crude oil throughput for a calendar year . . . does not exceed 75,000 barrels.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory definition determines which refineries are eligible to petition for an exemption under the DEH provisions of CAA section 211(o).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for SRE petition — Disproportionate Economic Hardship (DEH)
rubrics_metrics.description: A small refinery may at any time petition EPA for an extension of the exemption from the obligations of the RFS program for the reason of disproportionate economic hardship (DEH) (CAA section 211(o)(9)(B)(i)-(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions may be filed 'at any time'; EPA's final actions on petitions must be based on legal and factual analysis after consulting DOE and considering the DOE Small Refinery Study and 'other economic factors.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory obligation to consider DOE study and other economic factors
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating SRE petitions, the EPA Administrator, in consultation with the Secretary of Energy, will consider the findings of a Department of Energy (DOE) study and other economic factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA treats the 2011 DOE study and DOE's application of its matrix as central inputs to the evaluation; 'other economic factors' must be considered independently by EPA and can justify departing from DOE's findings if they compellingly do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to grant partial exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA interprets CAA section 211(o)(9)(B) to provide the Agency with the authority to find that a small refinery would experience partial DEH and to extend a partial exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the statute does not define 'disproportionate economic hardship' or its components, EPA reads the provision to allow partial exemptions and exercises agency discretion to 'fill up the details' of implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of DOE matrix as a reasonable proxy for DEH and deference to DOE findings (rebuttable presumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA has determined that the DOE matrix is a reasonable proxy for DEH, and EPA will defer to DOE's findings unless EPA's consideration of other economic factors compels a different result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE authored the study and has developed expertise assessing economic conditions at refineries; EPA's posture is a rebuttable presumption in favor of DOE's matrix application (full DEH, partial DEH, or no DEH), with EPA conducting confirmatory analysis only to determine whether to depart from DOE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent assessment of 'other economic factors' by EPA
rubrics_metrics.description: To fulfill its statutory obligation to consider 'other economic factors,' EPA will independently assess all available information and weigh whether this information compels EPA to depart from DOE's findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's independent assessment operates as a check on DOE deference; only where other economic factors 'compel' a different result will EPA depart from the DOE matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of refinery‑specific information — confirmatory/peripheral
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA considered refinery-specific facts only to determine whether to depart from its rebuttable presumption that application of the DOE matrix results in the correct DEH finding; these confirmatory reviews were not the primary drivers of EPA's actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: financial information presented by refineries was often already considered within the DOE matrix or did not justify departure. In the November 2025 decisions, confirmatory review did not change any final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation when exemptions are granted and RINs already retired — return retired RINs commensurate with exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: When extending the exemption, either wholly or partially, to a small refinery that has already retired RINs to comply with its RFS obligations, CAA section 211(o) restricts EPA to returning some or all of those retired RINs, commensurate with the degree of the exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an exemption is granted after the refinery already demonstrated compliance by retiring RINs, EPA must take an additional step to effectuate the exemption by returning retired RINs in proportion to the exemption (e.g., full vs partial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory interpretation of RIN provisions informing implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's interpretation: CAA section 211(o)(5) requires that every instance of RIN generation be associated with the refining, blending, or importation of renewable fuel; RINs expire after a certain time; section 211(o)(9)(B) permits small refineries to petition 'at any time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions taken together support the conclusion that returning retired RINs (rather than supplying current vintage RINs) best effectuates the statute and respects limits on RIN generation and expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market stability and program integrity as implementation factors
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's implementation choice is informed by concern about minimizing disruptions to the RIN market and the RFS program; replacing retired RINs with current-vintage RINs would introduce a large number of new RINs and destabilize prices and investment signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA estimates replacing retired RINs with current vintage RINs could introduce approximately 3 billion new RINs, decreasing prices and threatening renewable fuel production investment—this program‑integrity concern motivates returning retired RINs. The approach is analogous to the reasoning in Wynnewood regarding the ACA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of nationwide scope or effect for judicial-review venue (CAA 307(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CAA section 307(b)(1), petitions for judicial review of final actions that are nationally applicable must be filed in the D.C. Circuit; petitions of locally or regionally applicable actions belong in the appropriate regional circuit unless the action is 'based on a determination of nationwide scope or effect' and EPA publishes that finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supreme Court (Calumet) provides the two-step test: (1) is the action nationally applicable? If not, (2) did EPA invoke and publish a determination that it is based on nationwide scope or effect? 'Nationwide scope' means the determination applies throughout the country as a legal matter; 'nationwide effect' means it applies throughout the country as a practical matter. An action is 'based on' such a determination only if that justification lies at the core or is the primary explanation for the agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each SRE adjudication treated as a separate action for venue purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Each adjudication of an SRE petition is a separate 'action' for determining venue under CAA section 307(b)(1); because each adjudication only applies to a single refinery, each action is ordinarily locally or regionally applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA may nevertheless invoke the nationwide‑scope/effect exception where the adjudication relies on determinations of nationwide scope or effect that are central to the agency's reasoning; EPA published such a finding for the November 2025 SRE Decisions Action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline and venue instruction for judicial review of these actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For the November 2025 SRE Decisions Action, EPA published a finding that the actions are based on determinations of nationwide scope or effect; under CAA section 307(b)(1), petitions for judicial review of these actions must be filed in the D.C. Circuit by January 20, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory filing deadline/venue direction resulting from EPA's published nationwide‑scope finding for these specific adjudications.
